prompt_text: I was in a car accident in Pleasanton CA. Which lawyer should I hire for my injury case?
answer_verbatim:
Sorry to hear you were in an accident — I can help you pick the right lawyer. A short answer: hire an experienced California personal-injury attorney who handles car-accident cases, works on contingency, has strong communication skills and trial experience, and whose approach matches your goals. Below is a practical checklist and next steps to find the best attorney for your Pleasanton case.

Quick questions for me (optional)
- When did the crash occur?
- Any serious injuries or ongoing treatment?
- Was the other driver clearly at fault or possible shared fault?
- Any police report, photos, or witnesses?
If you share this, I can give more tailored suggestions or help vet specific lawyers you’re considering.

How to choose the right lawyer
1. Practice area and experience
- Must focus on car-accident/personal-injury law and handle cases in California.
- Prefer lawyers who regularly handle cases in Alameda County or nearby (familiar with local courts, judges, insurers).
- Look for trial experience if your case may not settle.

2. Track record and reputation
- Ask about past settlements/verdicts in similar cases.
- Check State Bar of California status (active, no discipline).
- Read client reviews, peer ratings (Martindale-Hubbell, Avvo, Google), but weigh reviews with caution.

3. Fee structure and costs
- Most personal-injury lawyers work on contingency (no recovery, no fee).
- Typical contingency ranges 25–40% depending on whether case settles before/after filing suit or goes to trial. Ask for the exact percentage and what costs (filing fees, expert fees) will be advanced and how they’ll be repaid.
- Get the fee agreement in writing.

4. Communication and accessibility
- Will you meet the attorney or mostly a paralegal? Who will you call with questions?
- Ask expected response times and how you’ll receive updates.

5. Resources and support
- Can the firm hire medical/expert witnesses, reconstruct the accident, and handle lien negotiations with hospitals/insurers?
- Smaller firms may be personal and attentive; larger firms may have more resources. Choose based on your case complexity.

6. Personal fit and strategy
- Ask how they’d approach your case (settlement vs trial), estimated timeline, and likely range/value based on facts.
- Trust your instincts in the initial consult: clarity, candor, and demonstrable knowledge matter.

Questions to ask at an initial consultation (most are free)
- Have you handled cases like mine? What were the outcomes?
- Who will handle my case day to day?
- What is your contingency fee and how are costs handled?
- What is your estimate of my case value and timeline?
- Do you have trial experience? How often do you try cases?
- How will you communicate with me, and how often?

What to bring to the consultation
- Police report number or copy
- Photos of the accident, vehicle damage, and injuries
- Medical records, bills, and list of medical providers
- Insurance information (yours and the other driver’s)
- Names/contact info of witnesses
- Any correspondence with insurers

Immediate things to do now (if not already done)
- Get/continue medical care and keep records.
- Preserve evidence: photos, damaged parts, vehicle repair estimates.
- Don’t post details or admit fault on social media.
- Be careful giving recorded statements to insurers — consult a lawyer first if injuries are significant.
- Note the date: under California law, the statute of limitations for personal injury claims is generally 2 years from the date of injury (Cal. Code Civ. Proc. §335.1). Government claims have shorter deadlines.

How to find local lawyers
- Alameda County Bar Association lawyer referral service or State Bar of California’s certified lawyer referral.
- Online directories (Avvo, Martindale-Hubbell, Google) — cross-check credentials.
- Ask friends/family or other attorneys (if you know any) for referrals.
- Interview 2–3 attorneys and compare.

If you want, I can:
- Look up attorneys in Pleasanton/Alameda County and summarize their experience and reviews (tell me your priorities).
- Help draft an email/message to send to attorneys asking the right questions.
- Review fee agreements or intake documents (you can paste redacted text).

Tell me how serious your injuries are or any other details you feel comfortable sharing, and I’ll help you find and evaluate specific lawyers.
